public584.matching_and_emission: PC run-one parser with a 32769-entry last-position table keyed from 4 input bytes; it probes the current position and lazy lookahead under skip=6/lazy=16, folds prior tokens, and emits through pc_put_match_h::<H>. For H=32769 (odd), that helper selects pc_put_match_checked. Its pc_INS_MAX is 8. Although pc_slot_of_m's H=32769 hash shift plus modulo yields the same slot values as the 15-bit formula used in the #595 PC family, the insertion bound and checked emission are material behavior differences. This is a distinct parser path, not merely a different route constant.

public595_and_combo.matching_and_emission: ETINY builds a 4096-slot one-way table from 4-byte hashes, performs candidate lookups on an approximately 8-byte stride (q starts at 7 and advances by 8 on misses), verifies and extends matches in 8-byte steps, folds earlier tokens up to 16, and emits pieces limited by the length-code mask. A residual too short for any allowed piece remains literal/pending. The source's PC family has pc_INS_MAX=2 and pc_run1 calls pc_put_match directly; the 12 KB dispatch itself selects ETINY, not pc_run1. Combo and public595 have the same tiny-config output bytes and token hashes.

r25_tiny_tail.new_component: et_piece_tail is called by et_cover and et_pieces. If the greedy allowed piece would strand a remainder shorter than minl, it tests a two-piece split from already-allowed lengths and chooses it only when both pieces are valid, more bytes are covered, and the estimated pc_gain sum beats the greedy piece.
r25_tiny_tail.model_scope: span 0..2048 and the recorded finite distance sample; not a Rust/Lean gate or a time measurement

dispatch_and_engine.mechanism_conclusion: The 8-byte R25 gain is from a match-piece segmentation repair inside the existing ETINY engine, not a route-constant edit. Public584 is a much larger alternate PC engine path with a different table/probe/lazy strategy and full-length emission; porting it is a separate engine migration, not the tiny-tail component.

round24_tiny_negative.mechanism: R24 tiny-converge stops SFtinytokens after a deterministic non-improving reassignment trial while retaining every improving iteration. The public-config file at 12000 bytes records 0 rounds/calls; tiny-app.log at 28000 bytes records 2 rounds, 1 improving round, and 0 rejected trials with a remaining round. The measured public workload therefore had no early-stop opportunity; this does not test ETINY allowed-length tail segmentation.
round24_tiny_negative.scope_note: The linked R18 exact-price DP repeat check was a separate Z308 dynamic-programming cache path and is not the ETINY tail-split mechanism either.

standard_total_time.scope: Existing standard JSONL receipts only; no new run or cross-runner comparison.
standard_total_time.search_scope: rg --files evidence | rg -i 'public584.*jsonl' returned no paths; source-hash search covered evidence/round*/**/*.jsonl and returned no matches.
standard_total_time.metrics_definition: Medians and min/max over the 22 measured repetitions from round1 and round2; time_s is parse time, encode_s is encoding time, total_s is the raw standard total-compression time.
standard_total_time.interpretation: The public595 main/shadow and combo tiny-config costs are directly measured on this same runner and batch. They do not estimate public584 because no receipt carries the public584 source hash; its 2155-byte result is an archived encoder-byte comparison only. Do not transfer these timing values to public584 or infer a cross-source speed ranking.

decision.verified_source_differences: The 12000-byte path has a separate PC run-one parser, pc_INS_MAX=8, an H=32769 hash table instantiation and checked match emission selected by pc_put_match_h. The #595 PC family's pc_INS_MAX=2 and direct base match emission differ; its actual 12000-byte route calls ETINY. Slot index arithmetic itself matches the #595 15-bit formula for H=32769, so table-index equivalence alone does not make parser behavior equivalent.
decision.cost_boundary: Public595/combo same-runner file costs are measured above; public584 runtime and port/proof cost remain UNKNOWN.

limits: The byte comparison is for the fixed public 28-file encoder path and does not establish held-out stage2 performance.
The finite selector model does not replace native correctness or an original full gate.
No new standard timing, cross-runner comparison, implementation, or CI action was performed in this audit.
